title: Multitask neural screening identifies four experimentally active antitrypanosomal hits
summary: Multitask neural activity models guided identification of four experimentally active compounds. This record represents the antitrypanosomal assay result, not four unprecedented chemical entities. LC-15 also appears in a later Leishmania study, which is a separate measured result.
ai_technology: Multitask feedforward and message-passing neural networks
organization: Federal University of Goiás; University of Brasília

evidence.tested: The primary abstract reports four experimental hits. Official supplementary computational tables compare multitask classification/regression with single-task baselines.
evidence.unknown: Main article Methods were inaccessible; operational assays were not reviewed. No mechanism, animal or clinical efficacy, absolute chemical novelty, or independent replication is claimed. Publisher online September 13 differs from the August issue date in indexing metadata.
evidence.ai_role: Multitask neural models learn compound activity across related tasks and prioritize experimental candidates.

source_review.scope: Primary abstract/front, fresh bibliographic status metadata and official supplementary computational tables. Previously reviewed exact LC-15 identity comparison reused without reopening structures or procedures.
